source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habitat: Swamps, stream banks and sites with frequent standing water; often acidic soils
morphology_documented.comparisons: Flora contrasts Q. macrocarpa, generally in at least moderately drained calcareous soils; moisture and soil differences are explicitly noted

regional_flora_key_traits.leaves: Deeply unevenly lobed with smaller terminal lobe than bur oak; pointed lobes (genus white-oak key)
regional_flora_key_traits.fruit: Mature acorn enclosed >3/4 by thin shell-like cup, cup opening usually <1/2 acorn diameter; cup <=3 cm diameter (genus key)

source_scope_note: Species, genus-key and secondary-source material separated; blank traits are not inferred from existing site data.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: The species paragraph does not provide individual leaf or acorn measurements; do not attribute existing learner descriptions to Diggs without matching the key
Genus white oak key describes nearly enclosed acorn (>3/4) and deeply unevenly lobed leaves; source pp. 712–713, key-level evidence
preservation: Additive research record only; originals, prior morphology, photos, source credits, galleries unchanged
